subject: Clarify invoicing recipient and tax docs for co-sell listings across AWS/Azure/GCP

Subject: Marketplace listing — who receives invoice / tax docs?

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement is trying to finalize how Contoso Cloud will be billed for the co-sell listing across AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace. Two quick asks we need to close the PO: 

1) Which legal entity will Redwood invoice for usage that originates via the AWS listing vs. direct Redwood charges? Our buyers want to know whether they receive a marketplace invoice (AWS invoice) or an invoice directly from Redwood.
2) For tax purposes: Contoso is EU-headquartered and wants to know what documentation you need from them (W-9 vs W-8BEN-E for withholding, VAT reverse-charge evidence, local tax registration if applicable).

Can you send a short note of the invoice flows and a sample invoice for each marketplace path? Also, if there are additional proofs needed for EU reverse-charge, please list them.

Thanks — Luca Bianchi
Contoso Cloud — Procurement
procurement@contosocloud.com

PS — copying Emma from AWS to keep the marketplace integration team in the loop.

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — who receives invoice / tax docs?

Hi Luca — thanks for the question and for including the marketplace contacts. Short answers up front, then details below and attached samples.

Short summary:
- AWS Marketplace usage is invoiced by AWS (buyer receives AWS invoice). Redwood issues a separate monthly settlement/merchant invoice to the reseller/partner (when applicable) and can issue a customer-facing invoice only in cases where the customer purchases directly from Redwood (not via marketplace).
- For Azure Marketplace and GCP Marketplace there are similar marketplace-invoice flows (platform invoices the buyer). If Contoso purchases via a marketplace listing, Contoso will typically receive the marketplace's invoice; Redwood can provide a statement-of-usage and a settlement invoice to the partner channel.

Tax/documentation notes: 
- US tax: If Contoso is a non-US company, we expect a completed W-8BEN-E (not a W-9). If Contoso has a US entity and requests US-sourced payments, we would need a W-9 for that US entity.
- EU VAT / reverse charge: If Contoso is EU-headquartered and provides a valid VAT ID, we can apply reverse-charge accounting where applicable. We require: 
  * Copy of the VAT registration for the buyer entity (VAT number),
  * Evidence the transaction is B2B (PO + billing address + VAT ID),
  * If Azure/AWS/GCP are involved, marketplace rules can differ — we typically provide an evidence checklist which I attached.

Attached: sample Redwood settlement invoice, W‑9 template (for completeness), and EU reverse-charge evidence checklist.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Confirm whether Contoso will buy via AWS/Azure/GCP listing or directly on Redwood (this changes who issues the invoice).
2) If buying via marketplace, ask Contoso to send VAT number + business registration and we can confirm whether reverse-charge applies and what supporting docs to upload to your procurement system.
3) If Contoso prefers a consolidated invoice from Redwood (to avoid multiple line items across vendors), we can explore a marketplace passthrough arrangement but that requires partner contracting and a short legal addendum.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call to walk through specifics — Vanessa is copied and handles marketplace billing operations.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — who receives invoice / tax docs?

Hi Luca (and team),

Adding a bit more color from ops on the differences you might see on the buyer-side when using each marketplace: 

AWS Marketplace (standard listing):
- Buyer receives an invoice from AWS for the subscription/usage. AWS collects payment, remits the partner share via their payout process.
- Redwood provides a settlement invoice to the AWS reseller account (our partner) — not to the buyer — unless we have a separate contractual agreement to invoice the buyer directly.
- Tax impact: AWS typically collects VAT where required on the marketplace invoice. For EU reverse-charge to apply, the buyer must be a VAT-registered business and provide their VAT number to AWS; AWS supports passing VAT details through in many cases but we also ask buyers to send evidence to us for our records.

Azure Marketplace / GCP Marketplace:
- Similar pattern: the platform invoices the buyer. Rules differ slightly for VAT handling and withholding; we will include platform-specific notes in the checklist.

If Contoso wants Redwood to be the invoice recipient (so you only pay Redwood and receive a single invoice), the typical approaches are:
1) Direct purchase (customer buys direct from Redwood) — buyer gets Redwood invoice; or
2) Partner consolidation (partner/reseller purchases on behalf of the buyer and then Redwood invoices partner; partner invoices buyer) — requires reseller agreement and mapping of legal entities.

For procurement teams: the practical doc we need from you is: the exact legal name and tax IDs for the buying entity (which entity on the PO will be billed), plus the purchase path (AWS listing vs Azure vs direct). Once we have that, we can produce the correct sample invoice + required evidence list.

I'll note one operational quirk we see frequently: some buyers want to claim VAT reverse-charge but the marketplace has already collected VAT at point of sale. In those cases the buyer needs a refund from the marketplace — which is operationally cumbersome. That's why many larger EU customers prefer direct purchase or partner consolidation.

Happy to set up a short call with Contoso procurement to review the checklist and tick the boxes.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Channel Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — who receives invoice / tax docs?

Thanks Olga and Vanessa — that helps. A couple follow-ups from our side after reviewing the sample invoice: 

1) Contoso's buying entity is: Contoso Cloud Solutions Ltd (UK registered) — VAT GB123456789. They will purchase via AWS listing.
2) For our PO we need to confirm which document to attach so our accounts payable will accept an "outgoing" invoice and apply reverse-charge. Should we attach Redwood's settlement invoice or will AWS provide the VAT-handled invoice acceptable for reverse-charge?

Contoso really wants to avoid the scenario where AWS collects VAT and there's no way for us to treat it as reverse-charge. If the marketplace collects VAT at purchase, they lose the reverse-charge treatment. Is there a recommended procurement path (direct or through a reseller) to ensure Contoso can self-account for VAT?

If needed we can provide our company registration cert and VAT record — what specific field formats/exports do you need for your records?

Best,
Luca

Hi Luca — quick operational recommendation and checklist to move this to close: 

Recommendation based on Contoso being UK VAT-registered and buying via AWS: 
- Preferred: If Contoso needs to self-account via reverse-charge, we recommend purchasing direct (Redwood invoice) or via a reseller partner who can issue a net invoice (partner invoices Contoso, Redwood invoices partner). Purchasing directly through AWS Marketplace often results in AWS charging VAT at checkout (marketplace-collected VAT), which prevents reverse-charge unless the marketplace supports business-to-business VAT exemption flows and the buyer provides VAT info at purchase.

Checklist of documents we need from Contoso to validate reverse-charge / B2B status and to keep on file: 
- Company legal name exactly as on registry (Contoso Cloud Solutions Ltd)
- VAT registration number (GB123456789) — we need a screenshot or PDF of the VAT registration page from HMRC or an official certificate
- Purchase order referencing the Redwood product SKU and the intended billing path (e.g., "Redwood direct invoice" or "AWS marketplace listing")
- Billing address and contact for AP

If you confirm that Contoso will still go through AWS and you'd like us to try to route a marketplace B2B flow, please ask Contoso to: 
- Enter their VAT number at the AWS checkout and ensure their AWS Marketplace account is set up as a business buyer; and
- Send us the VAT confirmation screenshot + PO. We'll coordinate with Emma at AWS to see if AWS will suppress VAT or allow reverse-charge for this transaction.

If you want a single consolidated Redwood invoice, we can prepare a reseller consolidation proposal (requires a short addendum so we can accept payment and remit via partner). If you'd like, I can draft the addendum template and loop in legal; Jordan is copied to help scope the reseller settlement terms.

Next step: Can you confirm the desired billing path by EOD Friday so we can produce the exact sample invoice and start the marketplace coordination? If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Emma from AWS to confirm marketplace VAT behavior for your account.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com
